name: Thymogen

lead: Thymogen is the brand name of a synthetic dipeptide, glutamyl-tryptophan, isolated from the calf thymus preparation Thymalin and then made synthetically. It is described as an immune system modulator.
Research is mostly animal and cell work from Khavinson's group; one rat study reported slower ageing and fewer spontaneous tumours. It has no documented appearance use.

paras: Reported to activate T-cell differentiation, alter intracellular cyclic nucleotides and activate neutrophil chemotaxis [1]. It has also been grouped among interferon-inducing immunomodulators developed in former socialist countries [2].
No systematic safety data in the sources; it is not approved in the US or EU.

lead: Thymogen is the brand name of a pharmaceutical based on the synthetic dipeptide L-Glu-L-Trp, which Khavinson's group isolated from the calf thymus extract Thymalin and then synthesised [1][2]. It is characterised as an immunomodulator.

Reported studies include a rat experiment in which the dipeptide was associated with slower ageing and inhibition of spontaneous carcinogenesis [2], and cell-culture work comparing it with other Khavinson peptides [3]. A review places it among interferon-inducing immunomodulators developed mainly in former socialist countries and little known in the West [4]. No link to appearance is documented.
infobox: Not approved in the US or EU as far as the sources show

paras: A 1997 review describes how Thymalin, a calf-thymus peptide complex, was used as an immunocorrector; the dipeptide L-Glu-L-Trp was isolated from it by chromatography, and Thymogen was designed on the basis of the synthesised dipeptide [1]. A second synthetic dipeptide, Vilon, followed [1].

The dipeptide was reported to activate T-cell differentiation and recognition, change cyclic nucleotide levels and stimulate neutrophil chemotaxis [2]. In rats it was reported to slow ageing and inhibit spontaneous tumour development [2]. A 2022 study in the THP-1 human monocyte/macrophage line compared Thymogen with Epitalon, Vilon, Thymalin and Chonluten for effects on proliferation and inflammatory pathways [3]. Other Russian-language reports include effects of thymus preparations on experimental tuberculosis [5] and on stress behaviour in mice when combined with other agents [6].
No studies found specific to Thymogen as a clinical trial in the sources reviewed. A Russian-language review summarises clinical results for peptide bioregulators as a class [7].

timeline.event: Review describes Thymogen as designed from the synthesised dipeptide L-Glu-L-Trp isolated from Thymalin [1].
Rat study reports slower ageing and fewer spontaneous tumours [2].
Compared with other Khavinson peptides in human THP-1 cells [3].
